before: inherit takes a property’s computed value from the parent, even for a property that normally does not inherit. initial uses the property’s specified initial value. unset chooses inheritance for inherited properties and the initial value for other properties.

Color normally inherits; padding does not. In this page, color: unset takes teal from the parent, while padding-left: unset becomes its initial 0px. initial is not a promise to restore a browser’s complete default stylesheet. These keywords affect the named property, not every style on the element.

Keep inherited teal text but remove the child’s own left padding using unset. The supplied HTML stays in index.html; edit the CSS. The checks inspect this small page, not every possible browser or accessibility requirement.
after: `inherit` copies a property’s final value from the parent. It works even for a property that does not usually pass from parent to child. This changes only the property you name.

`initial` uses the starting value defined for that CSS property. It does not restore every browser style. `unset` chooses between two actions: inherit a property that normally inherits, or use its initial value otherwise.
The parent still has its own padding. Removing the child’s padding does not remove the parent’s. Even if the parent’s left padding becomes 30 pixels, the child’s own padding stays at 0 with `unset`.
